    "file": "t60.py",

    "evidence": "Article.objects.raw(f\"SELECT id, title, published FROM blog_article WHERE author = '{author}' ORDER BY published DESC LIMIT {limit}\")",
    "llm_reasoning": "The code uses f-string interpolation to build a raw SQL query. Beyond the critical security risk (SQL injection), this bypasses Django's ORM query optimization and parameterization. Using raw SQL for simple filtering is unnecessary and prevents the database from effectively caching query plans for different author values. Furthermore, if the 'author' field is not indexed, this query will perform a full table scan on every request.",
    "suggested_fix": "Use the Django ORM: Article.objects.filter(author=author).order_by('-published')[:limit].values('id', 'title', 'published')",

    ]

    "issue_type": "Inefficient Data Serialization",
    "severity": "medium",
    "file": "t60.py",
    "line": 14,
    "evidence": "payload = [{'id': a.id, 'title': a.title, 'published': a.published.isoformat()} for a in articles]",
    "llm_reasoning": "The code fetches full model instances (including fields not needed) and then iterates over them in Python to build a dictionary. This is memory-intensive for large result sets. Using .values() or .values_list() in the ORM allows the database to return only the required columns, reducing memory overhead and serialization time.",
    "suggested_fix": "Use .values() to fetch only required fields: Article.objects.filter(author=author).values('id', 'title', 'published')",
